title: How the Goldkette band sounded and its audiences
summary: He describes the band playing all kinds of music, starting with the drums and others joining in, and playing for a crowd that listened.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Do you have any memories of the way your band sounded?
Tell me. Tell me what kind of a band. Was it a fast playing band? Did they play all kinds of music?
They played all kinds of music.
We would start playing and then everyone else would come in, you know.
You mean you'd start as a solo?
Then everyone else would come in with little inklings, you know.
Uh huh, okay. It was a band with a strong beat, obviously if you were the drummer, it had a strong beat.
Was it a kind of band in those days where people stood around and watched or did they dance or both? You know sometimes people will stop dancing.
What kind of a crowd did you usually get, the crowd that listens or the kind of crowd that danced?
And was that true even when you left Detroit and went to other cities?
